evidence.claim: Quanta states that its electric power capabilities include transmission line construction and maintenance, substation construction and maintenance, distribution line construction and maintenance, energized services, EPC, emergency restoration, program management, design, permitting, and materials management.
MYR Group describes itself as a holding company of specialty contractors serving electric utility infrastructure and commercial and industrial construction markets in the United States and Canada.

MYR Group's annual report describes the company as specialty electrical construction service providers with Transmission and Distribution and Commercial and Industrial segments; T&D customers include investor-owned utilities.

Primoris says its Power Delivery services include engineering and design, installation and maintenance, material and equipment procurement, and repair of electrical transmission, distribution, substation, wireless communication, and storm restoration assets.
Primoris describes its Utilities segment as building and maintaining utility infrastructure and says it is a full-service power delivery contractor serving the electric and communications industries.
NV5 describes itself as a provider of tech-enabled engineering, testing, inspection, and consulting solutions for the built environment, with utility services and power-related capabilities.

NV5's company profile lists power delivery, site inspections, audits, construction materials testing, engineering, geotechnical consulting, technical outsourcing, utility services, and geospatial markets among its offerings and end markets.

memory_update.text: PWR is the reference leader for the grid EPC labor and utility field-services node, but its mega-cap size and high attention make it more useful as a benchmark than an underfollowed discovery target.
MYRG is a strong underfollowed candidate for T&D specialty electrical construction exposure, especially if filings confirm durable T&D backlog, utility MSAs, and margin stability.

PRIM is a plausible underfollowed grid-services candidate through its Utilities/Power Delivery business, but later layers should separate power delivery from broader construction and gas utility exposure.
NVEE is a lower-attention testing/inspection/geospatial/utility-services hypothesis for the monitoring and commissioning side of the node; exposure purity needs verification before promotion.

Layer 1B found fewer pure-play public testing, protection-relay commissioning, drone inspection, and utility field-service companies than EPC contractors; many direct operators may be private, embedded in larger engineering firms, or hidden inside consulting/testing conglomerates.

node: Grid EPC labor, utility field services, testing, inspection, monitoring, and commissioning
summary: Layer 1B universe expansion for the grid EPC labor and utility field-services node identifies Quanta Services as the high-attention reference leader, with MYR Group, Primoris Services, and NV5 Global as more underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery candidates. The common chokepoint is not just grid capex, but the ability to deploy skilled crews, substation/transmission/distribution construction capacity, maintenance, inspection, testing, and project execution services needed to turn equipment orders into energized infrastructure. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
